According to IDC's latest report, although Mac shipments fell 11% in the third quarter of 2026, against a backdrop of an overall market shipment plunge of 20.1%, Apple's market share still rose from 8.5% to 9.5%. Here's the full rundown.

Apple still performed better than most of the PC market in a challenging environment

IDC today released its global PC shipment report for the third quarter of 2026, noting that while Mac shipments were down year-over-year, the company clearly outperformed the broader market.

According to IDC's preliminary data, Apple shipped a total of 5.9 million Macs in the third quarter of 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million a year earlier.

However, the decline across the overall PC market was even more pronounced, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-over-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

This performance kept Apple firmly in fourth place. The top three were, in order: market leader Lenovo, with 14.9 million units shipped and 23.8% market share; HP, with 10.3 million units and 16.5%; and Dell, with 7.6 million units and 12.1%.

Among the top five brands, HP saw the largest year-over-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS posted the smallest drop, down 8.6% year-over-year, shipping 5.5 million units for an 8.7% market share.

Looking ahead, IDC noted that "with high inventory and high prices, channel concerns about weak demand could trigger promotions in the near term," adding that "prices will remain well above last year's levels."

The firm also said the economy has weakened since the previous quarter, which could further dent demand, making "the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and into 2027 even darker."
